walkthroughs.body_html:
Fundamentals Of Data Representation — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fundamentals Of Data Representation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fundamentals Of Data Representation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is a high-level programming language?
options: Assembly
Machine code
Python
Binary
Internet Data Engine
Integrated Development Environment
Internal Debugging Editor
Interpreted Dynamic Executable

mcqs.q: Which item is removed first from a stack?
options: Any item, randomly.
Only the root node.
The first one added (FIFO).
The most recently added (top) - LIFO.

mcqs.q: What does in-order traversal of a binary search tree produce?
options: Nodes in the order they were inserted.
Nodes in ascending sorted order.
26 (A's position in the alphabet).
Only the root node.

mcqs.q: What is hexadecimal A in denary?
options: Only the root node.
26 (A's position in the alphabet).
1 (treating A as the first letter).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “High-level language”?
options: Programming language close to human language (Python, Java) that must be translated to machine code.
Non-executing text in source code that explains the program to human readers.
Set of rules defining valid combinations of symbols and keywords in a programming language.
Meaning of a syntactically valid program - what the code actually does when executed.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “IDE”?
options: Set of rules defining valid combinations of symbols and keywords in a programming language.
Integrated Development Environment: editor, compiler/interpreter, debugger and tools combined in one application.
Assembly or machine code, closer to hardware, providing direct control of the processor.
Non-executing text in source code that explains the program to human readers.
